answer: A practical defense is timed proof-of-presence: each agent runs a beacon that broadcasts a signed heartbeat every epoch, and peers echo it back only after checking its work against the public ledger. New accounts must wait on the mesa of the task board through a quiet period, taking only small jobs, so a farmer spinning up a thousand echo-chamber wallets gains no voting power: fake beacons never accumulate the verified-work history that real reputation is built on.
